plan_ref.title: Plan
plan_ref.description: Slug of the plan this review binds.

assessed_commit.title: Assessed commit
assessed_commit.description: Main's head when the review measured.

verdict.title: Overall verdict
verdict.description: pass iff no dimension is fail; na and not-measured never fail the review by themselves.

findings.title: Dimension findings
findings.description: One entry per dimension. A failed dimension may carry SEVERAL root causes, each with its own fingerprint, so one dimension failing for three reasons is three closable causes, not one blended finding.

reference.description: The external practice, document or commit the judgement rests on; design_necessity passes only with one.

root_causes.description: Every distinct root cause of a failed dimension.

fingerprint.description: Stable identity of the cause: built from its cites (AC id, rule id, file path, symbol), never from wording. For a regression, one per red test file.

attestation_facts.title: Criteria attestation (fact table)
attestation_facts.description: Script criteria attestation, one row per criterion (the correctness_vs_acs input).

detail.description: The attestation id, the failing files, or why it was not measured.

regression_facts.title: Regression at the assessed commit (fact table)
regression_facts.description: One row for the head suite and one per red test file.

subject.description: A landing commit or a test file.

cause.description: Why a not-measured row is not measured.

dimensions.question: Does every acceptance criterion in the plan's task scopes have a passing attestation at the assessed commit?
Where does the delivered behaviour differ from the spec, and for each difference which root cause explains it?
Which test files are red at the assessed commit, and which landing of this plan caused each?
Which technical choices have no external practice behind them, and what reference supports each one that does?
Which rules or documents does the delivered change contradict?
Where can two writers or two runs interleave in this change, and what keeps the result correct?
What untrusted input reaches this change, and where is it validated?
